questions.q: What Apex method publishes a custom platform event?
options: Database.insert(event)
EventBus.publish(event)
RestContext.publish(event)
Limits.publish(event)
questions.explain: EventBus.publish() publishes one or more platform event instances, accepting either a single event or a list.

questions.q: Under the Publish After Commit behavior, what governor limit does each EventBus.publish() call count against?
options: The 100-callouts-per-transaction limit
The regular Apex DML statement limit, checkable with Limits.getDMLStatements()
A dedicated 150-call Publish Immediate limit
There is no limit under Publish After Commit
questions.explain: Publish After Commit calls count as a DML statement against the standard DML statement limit, distinct from the separate 150-call limit for Publish Immediately.

questions.q: What does EventBus.publish() do when a publish is unsuccessful?
options: It throws a CalloutException
It throws a DmlException
It does not throw an exception at all — the caller must check the returned Database.SaveResult's isSuccess() and getErrors()
It automatically retries the publish up to three times
questions.explain: EventBus.publish() does not throw for a failed publish; failures must be detected by inspecting the returned SaveResult directly.

questions.q: What recursion risk does Salesforce's documentation specifically warn about with platform events?
options: Publishing an event from a trigger on that same event object can create an infinite trigger loop and exhaust limits
Subscribing to an event from more than one trigger is not allowed
Platform events cannot be published from Queueable Apex
Publishing more than 100 events per day is blocked automatically
questions.explain: Publishing from a trigger associated with the same event object risks an infinite trigger loop, a documented recursion hazard to watch for explicitly.

questions.q: In what sense are platform events naturally bidirectional, unlike most mechanisms in this course?
options: They are not bidirectional — platform events are outbound-only

The same event definition and Pub/Sub API can serve as either an outbound channel (Salesforce publishes, an external system subscribes) or an inbound channel (an external system publishes, an Apex trigger subscribes)
Platform events require two separate Named Credentials, one for each direction
Bidirectional publishing requires the webservice keyword
questions.explain: Whether a given platform event flow is outbound or inbound depends entirely on who published it and who is subscribed, using the same underlying mechanism either way.
